candidates.help_semantics_verified: --max-len N [0]: maximum segment length in characters (0 = unlimited, the frozen default); --split-on-word [false]: split on word rather than on token
candidates.mechanism: Diagnosed failure is late-anchored/merged segment starts: 29/88 aligned pairs exceed 500ms with pair-cer 0.00 (text exact, only start times scatter +-2-6s). Saved r4 artifact shows 36/99 segments exceed 8 chars (up to 20 chars / 7240ms). Capping segment length at 8 chars with word-boundary splitting forces merged segments to split, so each split piece re-anchors its start at word-level timing nearer the actual content instead of inheriting the merged segment's late start.

predicted_effect.cer: neutral (same decoded tokens, re-segmented; small two-sided risk if splits alter alignment edges)
predicted_effect.duplicated: neutral to slight-up risk (more hypothesis pieces could near-match an already-paired reference as a repeat; the segmentation_split_count diagnostic may absorb this instead, which is not counted)
predicted_effect.omitted: neutral to slight-up risk (re-segmentation can only move pairing edges, not delete content)
predicted_effect.timestamp_p95_ms: DOWN (primary hypothesis; expected material reduction but unlikely to reach <=500 alone)

candidates.help_semantics_verified: --best-of N [5] / --beam-size N [5]: frozen defaults already 5, so the task-suggested 5/5 would be a no-op rerun; widening to 10/10 is the minimal non-default decode-robustness step. --temperature stays frozen at 0.000. --word-thold deliberately untouched: it gates token-level timing only, while frozen scoring uses segment offsets. --vad-model/--dtw NOT used (unpinned). No condition_on_previous_text flag exists in this CLI build.
candidates.mechanism: Segment start/end times come from the decoder timestamp tokens ([_TT_*] sequence). A wider beam (10 vs frozen 5) searches more decode hypotheses, giving the timestamp-token placement more chances to land on the true onset; this is an INDIRECT mechanism (better token sequence -> better timestamp tokens), hence lower confidence than candidate A. best-of is raised alongside beam-size to keep the candidate-keeping width consistent with the wider beam.

predicted_effect.cer: neutral to slight-down (wider search can only keep equal-or-better scoring sequences under the same temperature)
predicted_effect.timestamp_p95_ms: DOWN slightly or NEUTRAL (low confidence; indirect mechanism). Wall time expected up roughly with beam width — reportable latency data; a run exceeding 10 min is itself a finding.

decision_rule: Per candidate: IMPROVED p95 (materially lower; success = <=500) or DISCARD. If both discard, stop — no third trial. Gate thresholds, measurement code, product argv template, reference file, and private/ inputs are never modified.

Whisper segment-timestamp imprecision (merged/late-anchored starts), NOT mishearing.
run_rules: Throwaway runs only: whisper-cli output goes to /tmp (never into private/ or the repo).
No frameworks, no permanent tests, no product code changes.
Zero paid API calls; whisper runs are local/free.
Exactly 2 candidates, run in sequence (parallel whisper-cli runs would oversubscribe the pinned --threads 4 CPU profile).

Convert each candidate JSON-full output to hypothesis shape (segments offsets start/end ms + text), apply production processing exactly (substituted_arm_transcript with episode_root, speech via segments_from_ms(segments_ms, 8467)), score with compute_arm_evidence_quality.
Per candidate also report: wall time, segment count, top-8 remaining pair deltas via align_utterances.
